correctness.rationale: The function 2u/sin(u) increases strictly from 2 to pi, so each 2<kappa<pi yields unique u. Directly substituting opposite two-block phases gives a literal least-period-two orbit; both Jacobians are the same symmetric block matrix because cos is even. Its eigenvalues on common rotation, inter-block, and intra-block zero-sum subspaces are respectively 1, 1-kappa*cos(u), 1-kappa*(p+q*cos(u)) (m-1 times) and 1-kappa*(q+p*cos(u)) (N-m-1 times). Floquet eigenvalues are their squares, and the singleton missing-mode cases do not undermine the criterion. Transverse attraction iff max(p,q)<p*=(sin(u)-u*cos(u))/(u*(1-cos(u))); > gives unstable eigenvalue, equality neutral +1 only. Integral p*=integral(s*sin(us))/integral(sin(us)), covariance of s and s*cot(us) strictly negative, gives 2/3 down to 2/pi; n=3 uniquely obstructed. Independently evaluated 21 original map/Jacobian cases.
